_notes: VCST-5748 OTP email sign-in — env-INDEPENDENT request inputs (no entity, nothing seeded). Consumed as @td(OTP_INPUTS.<field>) by suites 104 (storefront) and 105 (API). Drift guard: node scripts/seed-data/auth/validate-otp-signin-data.mjs. {{VAR}} tokens resolve from the layered .env at run time. LIMITS: the long-address pair is valid in every respect except LENGTH (64-char local part, 63-char labels), so a 254 accept / 255 reject split can only be caused by the MaxLength(254) rule — never by EmailAddress syntax; the 255 value also exceeds RFC 5321 so a client-side validator may reject it first (that is a legitimate outcome, record which layer refused it).
unknownEmail_note: NOT a literal address: generate a fresh one per run with scripts/lib/random-data.ts uniqueEmail("agent-test-otp-unknown") -> agent-test-otp-unknown-<ts>-<id>@qa.test. A fixed address could be registered by someone later and silently turn the masking case into a real-account case.

boundary.maxLength254_note: CONTROL for tooLong255 — identical shape, one character shorter. Must NOT be refused for length; it is an unregistered address, so the API answer is the unknown-email outcome, not a validation error.

missingParamBodies._notes: request_* go to POST {{BACK_URL}}/api/otp/request as JSON; grant_* go to POST {{BACK_URL}}/connect/token as application/x-www-form-urlencoded. grant_no_storeId / grant_no_email carry a deliberately WRONG code 000000 against {{USER_EMAIL}}: if the handler ever verified the code before rejecting the missing parameter it would register a failed attempt on a SHARED persona — run these only after the handler is confirmed to refuse on the missing parameter first.
